(idempotent re-issue) or\n      // when a tolerant compensation command (FailProvisioning) is invoked from\n      // a non-authorized state — persist nothing and emit no status-change event\n      // so the receipt still succeeds without a spurious transition.\n      if (!transition) {\n        return {\n          operationId: command.operationId,\n          tenantId: command.tenantId,\n          status: tenant.status,\n          previousStatus,\n          reason,\n        };\n      }\n\n      tenant.status = targetStatus;\n\n      // Suspension audit trio (DB-ADMIN-HIGH-003): persisted atomically with\n      // the status write by the single writer of auth.tenants. The SUSPENDED\n      // transition records when/why/who (actor.id travels on every lifecycle\n      // command via AuthTenantCommandMetadata); the ACTIVE transition clears\n      // all three because an active tenant is, by definition, not suspended.\n      // Other targets (DEACTIVATED/ARCHIVED/…) deliberately leave the trio\n      // untouched so a tenant deactivated OUT of suspension keeps the audit\n      // trail of its last suspension.\n      if (targetStatus === TenantStatus.SUSPENDED) {\n        tenant.suspendedAt = new Date();\n        tenant.suspendedReason = reason ?? null;\n        tenant.suspendedBy = command.actor.id;\n      } else if (targetStatus === TenantStatus.ACTIVE) {\n        tenant.suspendedAt = null;\n        tenant.suspendedReason = null;\n        tenant.suspendedBy = null;\n      }\n\n      await manager.save(Tenant, tenant);\n\n      // Durable TenantStatusChanged, atomic with the status write. The local\n      // lifecycle handlers previously emitted nothing on transition (events\n      // were dropped on the live path); routing through auth_outbox here is\n      // the single emission point for all five lifecycle transitions and\n      // commits in the same SERIALIZABLE receipt transaction.\n      await this.outboxPublisher.enqueue(\n        {\n          ...createBaseEvent<TenantStatusChangedEvent>('TenantStatusChanged', command.tenantId, {\n            aggregateId: command.tenantId,\n            aggregateType: 'Tenant',\n          }),\n          previousStatus,\n          newStatus: targetStatus,\n          reason,\n        },\n        manager,\n        {\n          aggregateId: command.tenantId,\n          idempotencyKey: `${command.operationId}:${commandType}:TenantStatusChanged`,\n        },\n      );\n\n      // RBAC-HIGH-007: a transition OUT of the operational state (SUSPENDED /\n      // DEACTIVATED / CANCELLED / ARCHIVED / PURGED — anything the\n      // isLoginAllowed SSoT rejects) must terminate the tenant's live\n      // sessions NOW, not at natural token expiry. Before this, suspend\n      // flipped the status + emitted the event but revoked nothing: every\n      // logged-in user kept full access and silently rotated new tokens for\n      // the refresh-token lifetime (days). The refresh-token kill is atomic\n      // with the status write (same SERIALIZABLE receipt transaction — a\n      // rolled-back suspend revokes nothing). The tx-local tenant GUC gives\n      // the RLS policy on auth.refresh_tokens exactly this tenant's rows —\n      // tenant-SCOPED context, not a bypass; the lifecycle command arrives\n      // over NATS with no request tenant context.\n      if (!isLoginAllowed(targetStatus)) {\n        const userRows = this.rowsFromQuery<{ id: string }>(\n          await manager.query(`SELECT id FROM \"auth\".\"users\" WHERE \"tenantId\" = $1`, [\n            command.tenantId,\n          ]),\n        );\n        lockedOutUserIds.push(...userRows.map((row) => row.id));\n        if (lockedOutUserIds.length > 0) {\n          await manager.query(`SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant', $1, true)`, [\n            command.tenantId,\n          ]);\n          await manager.query(\n            `UPDATE \"auth\".\"refresh_tokens\"\n                  SET \"isRevoked\" = true, \"revokedAt\" = NOW(), \"revokedReason\" = $2\n                WHERE \"userId\" = ANY($1::uuid[])\n                  AND \"isRevoked\" = false`,\n            [lockedOutUserIds, `Tenant ${targetStatus}`],\n          );\n        }\n      }\n\n      return {\n        operationId: command.operationId,\n        tenantId: command.tenantId,\n        status: targetStatus,\n        previousStatus,\n        reason,\n      };\n    });\n\n    // Post-commit: cut LIVE access tokens fleet-wide via the shared Redis user\n    // blacklist (the gateway rejects blacklisted users on their next request).\n    // Deliberately outside the transaction — Redis is not transactional — and\n    // deliberately non-fatal per user: the durable guarantee is the in-tx\n    // refresh-token revocation above plus the refresh-path tenant gate; access\n    // tokens self-expire within their ≤15-minute TTL even if Redis is down.\n    for (const userId of lockedOutUserIds) {\n      try {\n        await this.userTokenRevocation.revokeUserTokens(userId);\n      } catch (err) {\n        this.logger.warn(\n          `Access-token blacklist failed for userId=${userId} after ${commandType} on tenant ${command.tenantId}: ${(err as Error).message}`,\n        );\n      }\n    }\n\n    return execution.result;\n  }\n\n  private async assertTenantTransition(\n    manager: EntityManager,\n    command: AuthTenantCommandMetadata,\n    authorizedSources: readonly TenantStatus[],\n    targetStatus: TenantStatus,\n    options: { allowMissing?: boolean; seed?: boolean; tolerant?: boolean } = {},\n  ): Promise<{ tenant: Tenant; transition: boolean }> {\n    const tenant = await manager.findOne(Tenant, {\n      where: { id: command.tenantId },\n      lock: { mode: 'pessimistic_write' },\n    });\n\n    if (!tenant) {\n      if (options.allowMissing) {\n        return {\n          tenant: manager.create(Tenant, { id: command.tenantId, status: targetStatus }),\n          transition: true,\n        };\n      }\n      throw new NotFoundException(`Tenant with ID \"${command.tenantId}\" not found`);\n    }\n\n    // Idempotent re-issue: the tenant is already at the desired end-state — a\n    // success no-op (retried ActivateTenant on an ACTIVE tenant, re-issued\n    // FailProvisioning on an already-PROVISIONING_FAILED tenant), not a\n    // transition. From a state it\n      // is not authorized to fail (PENDING never provisioned, ACTIVE already\n      // succeeded) it is a no-op, not an error — the run-level FAILED state\n      // already records the failure.\n      if (options.tolerant) {\n        return { tenant, transition: false };\n      }\n      throw new BadRequestException(\n        `Tenant ${command.tenantId} is ${tenant.status}; this command requires one of ` +\n          `[${authorizedSources.join(', ')}] to reach ${targetStatus}`,\n      );\n    }\n\n    // Edge-legality SSoT (MT-HIGH-003): the canonical TenantStatusMachine is the\n    // single authority on whether from->to is a legal lifecycle transition. The\n    // authorizedSources above are a subset of its incoming edges, so this only\n    // ever throws on real drift; wrap its Error in a 400 so a caller-illegal\n    // transition stays a client error rather than a 500.\n    try {\n      assertTransition(tenant.status, targetStatus);\n    } catch (error) {\n      throw new BadRequestException(\n        `Invalid tenant transition for ${command.tenantId}: ${tenant.status} -> ` +\n          `${targetStatus} (${(error as Error).message})`,\n      );\n    }\n\n    return { tenant, transition: true };\n  }\n\n  private async runWithReceipt<TResult>(\n    commandType: string,\n    command: AuthTenantCommandMetadata,\n    entityType: string,\n    work: (manager: EntityManager) => Promise<TResult>,\n    options: {\n      replay?: (manager: EntityManager) => Promise<TResult>;\n      toSummary?: (result: TResult) => unknown;\n      entityId?: (result: TResult) => string | null;\n    } = {},\n  ): Promise<TenantCommandReceiptExecution<TResult>> {\n    this.assertCommandMetadata(commandType, command);\n    const canonicalPayloadHash = this.hashCommandPayload(commandType, command);\n    const receiptIdempotencyKey = this.receiptIdempotencyKey(\n      commandType,\n      command,\n      canonicalPayloadHash,\n    );\n\n    return this.dataSource.transaction('SERIALIZABLE', async (manager) => {\n      // ORPHAN-CRITICAL-573 — bind the RLS tenant context before the FIRST\n      // statement of the receipt lifecycle.\n      //\n      // `auth.tenant_command_receipts` carries the standard isolation policy:\n      // a row is visible/writable only under `app.bypass_rls=on` or when\n      // `app.current_tenant` equals its `tenantId`. This transaction ran with\n      // NEITHER, so every INSERT here was refused — and because the receipt is\n      // written before any provisioning step executes, EVERY tenant creation\n      // failed at step zero. Production carried two tenants stuck in PENDING\n      // with no schema for months as a result.\n      //\n      // Tenant-SCOPED, not a bypass: the receipt belongs to exactly this\n      // tenant, so the policy is satisfied honestly rather than switched off.\n      // Third argument `true` makes the setting transaction-local, so a pooled\n      // connection cannot carry this tenant into the next caller's query -\n      // the failure mode that makes a bypass here unacceptable.\n      await bindTenantRlsContext(manager, command.tenantId, 'auth');\n\n      const receiptRowsRaw: unknown = await manager.query(\n        `SELECT \"payloadHash\", status, \"entityId\", \"resultSummary\"\n           FROM auth.tenant_command_receipts\n          WHERE \"operationId\" = $1\n            AND \"tenantId\" = $2\n            AND \"commandType\" = $3\n            AND \"idempotencyKey\" = $4\n          FOR UPDATE`,\n        [command.operationId, command.tenantId, commandType, receiptIdempotencyKey],\n      );\n      const receiptRows = this.rowsFromQuery<TenantCommandReceiptRow<TResult>>(receiptRowsRaw);\n\n      const existing = receiptRows[0];\n      if (existing) {\n        if (existing.payloadHash !== canonicalPayloadHash) {\n          throw new ConflictException(\n            `${commandType} idempotency key was reused with a different payload`,\n          );\n        }\n        if (existing.status === 'SUCCEEDED') {\n          if (options.replay) {\n            return {\n              result: await options.replay(manager),","numLines":300,"startLine":820,"totalLines":1434}}}

{\n  Entity,\n  Column,\n  PrimaryGeneratedColumn,\n  CreateDateColumn,\n  Index,\n  ManyToOne,\n  JoinColumn,\n} from 'typeorm';\n\nimport { User } from './user.entity';\nimport { Tenant } from ['token'], { unique: true })\n@Index('IDX_refresh_tokens_expires', ['expiresAt'])\n@Index('IDX_refresh_tokens_tenant', ['tenantId'])\n@Index('IDX_refresh_tokens_family', ['familyId'])\n@Index('IDX_refresh_tokens_token_id', ['tokenId'], {\n  unique: true,\n  where: '\"tokenId\" IS NOT NULL',\n})\nexport class RefreshToken {\n  @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid')\n  id!: string;\n\n  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 255 })\n  token!: string;\n\n  /**\n   * Non-secret lookup identity embedded into the rolling-compatible opaque\n   * transport. New tokens resolve exactly one row without scanning bcrypt\n   * hashes; NULL preserves bounded legacy-token compatibility during rollout.\n   */\n  @Column({ type: 'uuid', nullable: true })\n  tokenId?: string | null;\n\n  @Column({ type: 'uuid' })\n  userId!: string;\n\n  /**\n   * SECURITY (SEC-MEDIUM-003): rotation lineage id. A fresh login starts a\n   * NEW family; every rotation carries the SAME familyId forward. On\n   * reuse-detection the revocation is scoped to the suspect token's family\n   * (not the whole user) so a single stale-cookie replay does not nuke all\n   * of a user's other devices, and the emitted SecurityEvent carries a true\n   * family-id for incident correlation.\n   */\n  @Column({ type: 'uuid', nullable: true })\n  familyId?: string | null;\n\n  /**\n   * \"Remember me\" persistence flag. Set at fresh login from the client's choice\n   * and carried forward on every rotation (like familyId) so a remembered\n   * session stays persistent across silent refreshes. The resolver reads it to\n   * branch the refresh-cookie maxAge; token.service extends this row's expiresAt\n   * to the remember-me TTL when true so the persistent cookie never outlives it.\n   */\n  @Column({ type: 'boolean', default: false })\n  rememberMe!: boolean;\n\n  @ManyToOne(() => User, { onDelete: 'CASCADE' })\n  @JoinColumn({ name: 'userId' })\n  user!: User;\n\n  // DATA-MEDIUM-002: deliberately nullable. A SUPER_ADMIN / platform actor has\n  // NO tenant, so its refresh tokens legitimately carry NULL tenantId (mirrors\n  // auth.users.tenantId's documented platform-actor exception). A DB constraint\n  // cannot express \"non-null unless the owner is SUPER_ADMIN\" (cross-table), so\n  // the application contract sets tenantId for every tenant-scoped session.\n  @Column({ type: 'uuid', nullable: true })\n  tenantId?: string | null;\n\n  @ManyToOne(() => Tenant, { nullable: true, onDelete: 'SET NULL' })\n  @JoinColumn({ name: 'tenantId' })\n  tenant?: Tenant | null;\n\n  @Column({ type: 'timestamptz' })\n  expiresAt!: Date;\n\n  @Column({ type: 'boolean', default: false })\n  isRevoked!: boolean;\n\n  @Column({ type: 'timestamptz', nullable: true })\n  revokedAt?: Date | null;\n\n  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 255, nullable: true })\n  revokedReason?: string | null;\n\n  /** First-writer marker for idempotent refresh-token reuse containment. */\n  @Column({ type: 'timestamptz', nullable: true })\n  reuseContainedAt?: Date | null;\n\n  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 500, nullable: true })\n  userAgent?: string | null;\n\n  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 50, nullable: true })\n  ipAddress?: string | null;\n\n  @Column({ type: 'varchar', length: 100, nullable: true })\n  deviceId?: string | null;\n\n  @CreateDateColumn({ type: 'timestamptz' })\n  createdAt!: Date;\n\n  isExpired(): boolean {\n    return this.expiresAt < new Date();\n  }\n\n  isValid(): boolean {\n    return !this.isRevoked && !this.isExpired();\n  }\n}\n","numLines":115,"startLine":1,"totalLines":115}}}

],\n      \"rationale\": \"INDEPENDENT VERDICT: false_positive, reached from parameter provenance rather than from the absence of a tenantId column. WHAT THE RULE SAW, AND WHY THAT IS NOT THE REFUTATION. The raw UPDATE on auth.refresh_tokens at :945 selects rows with WHERE \\\"userId\\\" = ANY($1::uuid[]) AND \\\"isRevoked\\\" = false (:948) and names no tenant column. That syntactic match is CORRECT as an observation, so 'the rule matched literally' cannot by itself be the reason the finding is wrong; a raw statement against a tenant-bound table with no tenant predicate is exactly what this rule exists to surface. WHERE THE TENANT PREDICATE ACTUALLY LIVES. lockedOutUserIds is declared empty at :854's enclosing scope and is written in exactly one place, :940, from the rows of the SELECT at :936 - SELECT id FROM \\\"auth\\\".\\\"users\\\" WHERE \\\"tenantId\\\" = $1, bound to command.tenantId. The UPDATE's only free row-selector is therefore a value computed BY a tenant-equality predicate on the same tenant id. A user outside command.tenantId cannot enter the id set, so no row outside that tenant is reachable by the UPDATE. The tenant binding is present and is carried by the parameter instead of written into the WHERE clause - which is precisely the binding a pattern-shaped adapter rule cannot observe. TWO CHECKS I RAN RATHER THAN ASSUMED. (1) Divergent-tenant rows: auth.refresh_tokens carries its own nullable tenantId, so I asked whether a row could be stamped with a tenant other than its owner's. The user class whose token tenant can legitimately diverge is the platform actor whose auth.users.tenantId is NULL, and :936's \\\"tenantId\\\" = $1 never matches NULL, so that class is structurally excluded from the id set. (2) Direction of the operation: the statement REVOKES - it removes access and grants none. A tenant-isolation defect requires one tenant reaching another tenant's data; a revocation bounded by one tenant's own users cannot produce that outcome even if a row were mis-stamped. This makes the verdict robust to schema surprises I did not read. DEFENSE IN DEPTH, NOT THE BASIS OF THE VERDICT. The write runs inside the SERIALIZABLE receipt transaction opened at :1078 with the RLS tenant context bound at :1095 through the helper imported at :3, and :942 re-binds app.current_tenant transaction-locally before the UPDATE. I did not read the RLS policy DDL, so I rest the verdict on provenance (:936, :940, :948), which does not depend on those controls being correct. DO THE PRIOR VERDICTS SURVIVE. On direction, yes - with two qualifications the operator should see. First, the pair alone does not clear the aggregation bar: 0.6 and 0.93 give a mean of 0.765, under the 0.80 threshold; the three-judge mean including my 0.94 is 0.8233. My independent agreement, not the pair's, is what carries this to anchor grade. Second, neither quoted rationale completes the provenance chain: the adversarial judge's text enumerates what must be verified and stops at 0.6 without closing it, and the evidence judge's quoted fragment argues from the absence of the column. I reached the same verdict on a different and load-bearing basis, so this is agreement on the merits rather than ratification. ADJACENT OBSERVATION, RECORDED AS AN OBSERVATION AND NOT AS PART OF THIS VERDICT. Because refresh_tokens.tenantId is nullable and populated by application contract rather than by a database constraint, an RLS policy keyed on that column could hide a NULL-stamped row from this UPDATE and leave a suspended tenant's session live. That is an UNDER-revocation question - the opposite failure direction from the one this finding asserts - and it belongs to a separate finding class rather than to this verdict.\",\n      \"prior_verdicts\": [\n        {\n          \"judge_id\": \"aria-adversarial-judge\",\n          \"verdict\": \"false_positive\",\n          \"confidence\": 0.6,\n          \"arbiter_assessment\": \"Direction agreed; the quoted rationale states verification obligations without discharging them, and 0.6 is below the consensus bar.\"\n        },\n        {\n          \"judge_id\": \"aria-evidence-judge\",\n          \"verdict\": \"false_positive\",\n          \"confidence\": 0.93,\n          \"arbiter_assessment\": \"Direction agreed; the quoted rationale reasons from the missing column rather than from the id-set provenance that actually bounds the write.\"\n        }\n      ]\n    },\n    \"explanation\": \"WHY THIS ARBITRATION EXISTS AND WHAT BREAKS IF IT IS SKIPPED. When two judges agree, the kernel promotes that agreement to repository ground truth: it suppresses this finding class, can quarantine the rule that produced it, and scores the judges who voted. A third judge that merely restates the pair converts an unexamined agreement into a permanent blind spot - the adapter stops reporting this shape of query everywhere in the repository. So the mode asks for refutation, and disagreement is a real answer, because feedback_store.generate_ai_consensus counts the judges who AGREED with the settled verdict, not the judges who voted. THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON. A tenant predicate is not always a WHERE clause. Here it is the provenance of a bind parameter: the UPDATE at :945 is safe because its $1 was computed by a tenant-equality SELECT at :936 and written in exactly one place at :940. Any judgment of a 'missing tenant predicate' finding must therefore trace every free variable in the row-selector back to its source, and must ask which direction the statement moves access - a revocation bounded by one tenant's own users cannot leak across tenants even if its row set were imperfect. Stopping at 'no tenantId appears in the WHERE clause' decides the case on the same information the regex already had. DOWNSTREAM SURFACE AFFECTED. The raw UPDATE on auth.refresh_tokens at :945 selects rows with WHERE \\\"userId\\\" = ANY($1::uuid[]) AND \\\"isRevoked\\\" = false (:948) and names no tenant column. That syntactic match is CORRECT as an observation, so 'the rule matched literally' cannot by itself be the reason the finding is wrong; a raw statement against a tenant-bound table with no tenant predicate is exactly what this rule exists to surface. WHERE THE TENANT PREDICATE ACTUALLY LIVES. lockedOutUserIds is declared empty at :854's enclosing scope and is written in exactly one place, :940, from the rows of the SELECT at :936 - SELECT id FROM \\\"auth\\\".\\\"users\\\" WHERE \\\"tenantId\\\" = $1, bound to command.tenantId. The UPDATE's only free row-selector is therefore a value computed BY a tenant-equality predicate on the same tenant id. A user outside command.tenantId cannot enter the id set, so no row outside that tenant is reachable by the UPDATE. The tenant binding is present and is carried by the parameter instead of written into the WHERE clause - which is precisely the binding a pattern-shaped adapter rule cannot observe. TWO CHECKS I RAN RATHER THAN ASSUMED. (1) Divergent-tenant rows: auth.refresh_tokens carries its own nullable tenantId, so I asked whether a row could be stamped with a tenant other than its owner's. The user class whose token tenant can legitimately diverge is the platform actor whose auth.users.tenantId is NULL, and :936's \\\"tenantId\\\" = $1 never matches NULL, so that class is structurally excluded from the id set. (2) Direction of the operation: the statement REVOKES - it removes access and grants none. A tenant-isolation defect requires one tenant reaching another tenant's data; a revocation bounded by one tenant's own users cannot produce that outcome even if a row were mis-stamped. This makes the verdict robust to schema surprises I did not read. DEFENSE IN DEPTH, NOT THE BASIS OF THE VERDICT. The write runs inside the SERIALIZABLE receipt transaction opened at :1078 with the RLS tenant context bound at :1095 through the helper imported at :3, and :942 re-binds app.current_tenant transaction-locally before the UPDATE. THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON. A tenant predicate is not always a WHERE clause. Here it is the provenance of a bind parameter: the UPDATE at :945 is safe because its $1 was computed by a tenant-equality SELECT at :936 and written in exactly one place at :940.
